label: ua.news;Record gold decline fuels Bitcoin growth | UA.NEWS;https://ua.news/en/finansi/rekordne-padinnia-zolota-stimuliuie-zrostannia-bitkoina;2026-03-26T07:15:32.966000+00:00
text:
Record gold decline fuels Bitcoin growth
Gold has experienced a record decline for 10 consecutive days. Since the beginning of the year, the asset has dropped by 27%, and since the end of February, by about 12%. Against this backdrop, Bitcoin remains above $70,000, with its ratio to gold rising nearly 30%, reaching almost 16 ounces per 1 BTC compared to around 12 previously.
Source Incrypted
Bloomberg analyst Katy Greifeld considers that the market is currently undergoing a shift in focus: gold is gradually losing its "safe haven" status, and capital is moving from gold to Bitcoin, which is increasingly establishing itself as a protective asset.
In recent months, gold has shown significant volatility but now faces downward price pressure, boosting interest in alternative assets, especially cryptocurrencies. Meanwhile, Bitcoin’s crossing above $70,000 strengthens its position among investors as a potential "safe haven."
Bitcoin is a decentralized digital currency created in 2009, independent of governments and financial institutions. In recent years, it has gained popularity as a store of value, particularly amid economic uncertainty.
Thus, the record decline in gold may act as a catalyst for further Bitcoin strengthening. There is an ongoing redistribution of capital between traditional and digital assets.
Going forward, greater attention to cryptocurrencies as capital protection tools is expected amid global instability, while gold’s role may continue to gradually diminish.

label: ua.news;France completes repatriation of gold reserves from the US, gains over €13 billion | UA.NEWS;https://ua.news/en/finansi/frantsiia-povernula-svoyi-zoloti-rezervi-z-ssha-otrimavshi-ponad-13-mlrd-ievro-dokhodu;2026-03-26T07:15:39.106000+00:00
text:
France completes repatriation of gold reserves from the US, gains over €13 billion
The French central bank has finished repatriating its gold reserves previously stored in New York by selling 129 tonnes of bullion there and acquiring new gold in France. The process took place from July 2025 to January 2026, after which the gold was relocated to Paris. Due to high gold prices, the central bank recorded a one-time profit of nearly €13 billion (around $15.1 billion).
Following the freezing of Russia’s central bank reserves in 2022, the repatriation of gold became a prominent topic among central banks and governments. Countries like India and Serbia have already begun returning gold bullion, while Germany, Italy, Poland, and Romania have also called for gold repatriation.
The French central bank undertook this operation to safeguard its reserves and capitalise on the rising global gold prices, positively affecting its financial position.
Founded in the 19th century, the Bank of France is responsible for managing the country's monetary policy, including supervising official reserves such as gold and foreign currencies.
This move may signal a broader trend in Europe as nations seek to strengthen financial sovereignty and secure their assets amid geopolitical instability.
It is expected that other central banks will intensify efforts to repatriate gold to their jurisdictions, increasing transparency and influence in global gold markets.

ROCKFORD, Ill. (WREX) — First-time homebuyers are disappearing from the housing market, squeezed by rising prices and the growing challenge of saving for upfront costs.
According to the National Association of REALTORS, the share of first-time buyers fell to a historic low of 21% in its 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers, while the median age of those buyers climbed to a record 40.
The trend is playing out in Rockford, where home prices continue to reach new highs, leaving many younger buyers struggling to afford a down payment.
State housing officials say a new program aims to reverse that pattern.
Launched March 2 by the Illinois Housing Development Authority, the IHDA Access Forgivable Mortgage offers eligible first-time buyers up to 6% of a home’s purchase price — capped at $15,000 — to cover down payments and closing costs. The assistance is structured as an interest-free second mortgage that is fully forgiven after 10 years, with buyers required to contribute as little as 1% of the purchase price.
The $15,000 maximum is roughly double what previous statewide assistance programs have offered.
For lifelong Rockford resident Sue Levingston, the program provided an opportunity she felt she could not pass up.
“I've lived in Rockford all of my life, I jumped right on it as a first time home buyer,” Levingston said.
Levingston said the financial barriers to homeownership had felt increasingly difficult to overcome.
“Everything is more expensive, you know,” she said. “And so the challenge for me was, when it comes to your money, you want to make sure that I have enough to do what I need to do, so you work hard at it.”
The assistance helped bridge that gap.
“It's giving me an opportunity to go into a home with help on a down payment and with some of my closing and so that's very helpful for me, because it frees up extra money for me to be able to use in my own home,” she said.
Levingston said the program ultimately made homeownership attainable.
“It means the world to me to be able to have my own home,” she said. “I thought, you know, this is going to be one of the best things I could ever do for myself.”
Housing professionals say affordability remains the biggest obstacle for first-time buyers.
“The challenge is affordability,” said Realtor Staci Brown. “So you're going to hear a lot about affordability. Obviously, this year, it's a hot topic. So this first time home buyer grant is really going to help a lot of first time home buyers jump into the market with having access to assistance with their down payment and closing costs.”
Loan officer Erica Medrano said many potential buyers have steady incomes but struggle to save enough upfront.
“A lot of people have jobs. They make decent money, but it's saving up for that down payment. That can be a struggle,” Medrano said. “$15,000 is life changing money for a lot of people, so being able to use that for down payment and closing costs is what gets their foot in the door to be able to buy a home.”
Housing experts say the timing of homeownership can have long-term financial consequences. Delaying a home purchase from age 30 to 40 can cost a typical buyer as much as $150,000 in lost home equity.

text:

Silver Spot Price Hits $72.46 per Ounce on March 26, 2026: Recovery Gains Momentum Amid Iran Tensions and Fed Policy Watch
26.03.2026 - 08:15:36 | ad-hoc-news.deSilver spot prices have surged to $72.46 per troy ounce as of March 26, 2026, marking a $0.78 gain from the previous session and signaling a robust recovery for U.S. investors seeking inflation hedges and industrial exposure amid escalating geopolitical tensions.
As of: Thursday, March 26, 2026, 3:15 AM ET (7:15 AM UTC)
Spot Silver Rebounds Sharply After Volatile Week
The **spot silver** price reached $72.46 per ounce on March 26, 2026, reflecting a modest but significant bounce following a turbulent period of sharp declines. This level positions silver well above its recent lows around $70, with year-over-year gains exceeding $38 per ounce from March 2025 levels near $34. For U.S. investors, this development underscores silver's dual role as a safe-haven asset and key industrial metal, particularly as **COMEX silver futures** align closely with spot movements in regular trading sessions.
Trading data shows silver stabilizing after a 44% flash crash from its January 2026 high, exposing strains in the delivery system between paper contracts and physical metal. The rebound comes as **LBMA silver** benchmark contexts remain supportive, with no major divergences reported in recent sessions. U.S. market participants, focused on Eastern Time benchmarks, note the price uptick during early morning hours, equivalent to pre-market positioning ahead of the COMEX open.
Iran Crisis Fuels Geopolitical Risk Premium
A primary driver behind the silver price recovery is the ongoing Iran war, which began on February 28, 2026, pushing investors toward precious metals. Since the conflict's onset, silver has navigated volatility but held above key supports, with the current $72.46 spot level reflecting renewed risk aversion. The transmission mechanism is direct: heightened geopolitical instability boosts demand for non-yielding assets like silver, amplifying its sensitivity compared to gold due to its smaller market size.
For U.S. investors, this ties into broader energy market dynamics, as falling oil prices post-Iran escalations paradoxically support silver by easing inflation fears while sustaining safe-haven bids. COMEX futures, which dictate much of U.S.-listed ETF pricing, mirrored this upmove, with front-month contracts gaining in after-hours trading aligned with the spot lift.
Federal Reserve Policy Looms Large Over Silver Trajectory
U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate policy remains a pivotal factor, with the fed funds rate held at 3.50%-3.75% amid hawkish signals. Silver's inverse relationship with real yields means higher-for-longer rates pressure prices, yet the current rebound suggests dip-buying on expectations of eventual cuts. Mid-March stabilization around $77 per ounce, down from January peaks near $121, highlights this tug-of-war.
U.S. investors holding silver ETFs like SLV or physical bars should monitor upcoming FOMC minutes and economic data, as any dovish tilt could propel spot silver toward $80. The mechanism here is clear: lower yields reduce the opportunity cost of holding silver, spurring ETF inflows and physical demand from COMEX-registered warehouses.
Supply Deficits and Industrial Demand Bolster Bull Case
Beneath the surface volatility, structural supply deficits continue to underpin silver prices. Annual mine production lags consumption, particularly from solar panel manufacturing and electronics, where silver's conductivity is irreplaceable. The **silver market** faces persistent shortfalls, with 2025 deficits carrying into 2026, supporting prices despite paper market swings.
Solar demand, projected to consume record volumes, directly transmits to higher physical premiums over COMEX futures. U.S. investors benefit as domestic green energy incentives amplify this trend, positioning silver as a play on the energy transition. Recent data confirms no relief in sight, with recycling unable to bridge the gap.
Technical Levels and Trader Positioning in Focus
From a technical standpoint, silver has defended the $70 area as a floor, with short-term rallies probing resistance near $75. Analysts note force liquidations during last week's risk-off flush contributed to the drop below the 200-day EMA, but the bounce invalidates immediate downside risks toward $50. COMEX positioning shows speculators reducing net longs, creating room for further upside if physical delivery pressures mount.
The widening gap between paper silver (futures) and physical markets, highlighted in recent weeks, adds caution. U.S. traders watching CFTC Commitment of Traders reports will assess if commercials are absorbing supply, a bullish signal for spot silver sustainability.
U.S. Dollar Weakness Aids Silver's Advance
A softening U.S. dollar index has aided the silver rebound, as the metal's dollar denomination amplifies inverse correlation. Post-March 25 data, the dollar's retreat from recent highs—tied to Iran-related oil dynamics and rate hike bet reductions—directly lifts silver quotes. For U.S. investors, this interplay with the DXY is crucial, as sustained dollar weakness could mirror 2025's bull run.
Spot silver's 5.28% jump from $69.57 underscores this sensitivity, with intraday ranges of $71.31-$74.80 capturing the volatility. Broader precious metals rallied in tandem, but silver's outperformance reflects its beta to gold in risk-on recoveries.
ETF Flows and Investment Demand Signals
U.S.-listed silver ETFs saw modest inflows amid the rebound, with assets under management stabilizing after outflows during the correction. Instruments tracking COMEX futures, rather than pure spot, provide leveraged exposure but carry contango risks if backwardation emerges from physical squeezes.
For retail investors, the current setup favors accumulation at $72 levels, balancing industrial tailwinds against macro headwinds. Institutional flows, often leading spot moves, point to renewed interest as Iran tensions persist.
Outlook: Balancing Risks and Catalysts
Looking ahead, silver's path hinges on Fed rhetoric, Iran developments, and upcoming inflation prints. Upside targets near $80 loom if supports hold, while breakdowns below $70 reopen correction paths. U.S. investors should prioritize diversified exposure via ETFs or futures, mindful of leverage in volatile sessions.
MCX silver futures in India, at Rs 2,34,700 per kg (equivalent to roughly $72 aligned with spot), confirm global synchronization, though local premiums reflect physical hoarding.

text:
TOBACCO farmers have earned over US$74 million within the first two weeks of the 2026 marketing season, which reached its 11th day on Friday.
Latest statistics from the Tobacco Industry and Marketing Board (TIMB) show that more than 27 million kilogrammes of tobacco have been sold so far, a 44% increase from the 19 million kilogrammes delivered during the same period last year.
Premier Tobacco Auction Floor market analyst Sam Garaba said although the season initially was characterised by price fluctuations, the market was beginning to stabilise.
“The market has stabilised as farmers have started responding positively to market forces. Volumes have begun to increase after two weeks of price discovery and the season is now taking shape. We urge farmers to grade their leaf properly and deliver on time,” Garaba said.
Farmers expressed cautious optimism as prices begin to firm.
“We are confident that with the current situation, we are getting there, where every farmer will get a fair price for their leaf,” one farmer said.
“Although prices were very low at the beginning, they are firming now.”
Another farmer who delivered his crop earlier this week said his decision was informed by close monitoring of market trends.\
“I brought my tobacco for sale on Monday after studying the market and I believe I will get a good price based on current trends,” he said.
The average price stands at US$2,71 per kilogramme, down from US$3,50 during the same period last year.
However, despite softer prices influenced by global market conditions, the overall value of sales has risen by 12%, from US$66 million last year to over US$74 million this season, driven mainly by stronger volumes.

Here's What We Like About TOKAI's (TSE:9729) Upcoming Dividend
Readers hoping to buy TOKAI Corp. (TSE:9729) for its dividend will need to make their move shortly, as the stock is about to trade ex-dividend. The ex-dividend date generally occurs two days before the record date, which is the day on which shareholders need to be on the company's books in order to receive a dividend. The ex-dividend date is an important date to be aware of as any purchase of the stock made on or after this date might mean a late settlement that doesn't show on the record date. Accordingly, TOKAI investors that purchase the stock on or after the 30th of March will not receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 29th of June.
The company's next dividend payment will be JP¥34.00 per share, and in the last 12 months, the company paid a total of JP¥58.00 per share. If you buy this business for its dividend, you should have an idea of whether TOKAI's dividend is reliable and sustainable. So we need to investigate whether TOKAI can afford its dividend, and if the dividend could grow.
Dividends are typically paid out of company income, so if a company pays out more than it earned, its dividend is usually at a higher risk of being cut. TOKAI paid out a comfortable 35% of its profit last year. A useful secondary check can be to evaluate whether TOKAI generated enough free cash flow to afford its dividend. text:
India credit growth surges 61 pc in FY26: Report
By IANS | Updated: March 26, 2026 12:35 IST2026-03-26T12:33:31+5:302026-03-26T12:35:11+5:30
New Delhi, March 26 India’s credit growth has seen a sharp jump in FY26, rising 61 per cent, ...
New Delhi, March 26 India’s credit growth has seen a sharp jump in FY26, rising 61 per cent, driven mainly by strong demand from retail borrowers and MSMEs, a new report showed on Thursday.
Credit growth in India has accelerated significantly in FY26, with total credit flows rising to Rs 25.1 lakh crore, nearly matching deposit mobilisation of Rs 26.1 lakh crore, a report by Yes Bank said.
The report noted that strong demand across retail, MSME and infrastructure sectors has been the key driver of this growth.
However, deposit growth has been slowing since FY24, creating some pressure on liquidity in the banking system.
As a result, the credit-deposit (C/D) ratio has climbed to 82.4 per cent, its highest level in a decade.
Retail loans continue to dominate credit growth. Personal loans have seen their share rise from 29 per cent to 33 per cent in recent years, supported by tax relief measures and GST-related benefits that have boosted household incomes.
Within this segment, vehicle loans have emerged as the biggest driver, overtaking housing loans since the third quarter of FY26.
There is also a noticeable shift towards secured lending as growth in unsecured loans has slowed.
The report also highlighted a recovery in industrial credit, led by MSMEs. The segment now accounts for nearly one-third of total industrial credit and has seen strong growth due to government support, including credit guarantee schemes and revised MSME definitions.
Micro and small enterprises alone added Rs 2.38 lakh crore in loans during the year, while medium enterprises contributed Rs 63,000 crore, the report said.
Looking ahead, the report cautioned that credit growth may slow in FY27 due to several risks.
Higher oil prices, weaker exports and rising food inflation could impact economic activity and reduce demand for loans.
At the same time, the fading impact of GST benefits may also weigh on growth, the report stated.

text:
BY EDISON JOSEPH GONZALES
GT Capital Holdings Inc. posted a consolidated net income of P33.68 billion in 2025, up 17 percent from a year earlier.
Core net income rose 8 percent to P30.47 billion, driven by record profits at Metrobank and Toyota Motor Philippines (TMP), which reported P49.7 billion and P19.0 billion, respectively.
Associate Metro Pacific Investments Corp. (MPIC) contributed a consolidated core net income of P27.1 billion.
The board approved a P14.16 per share cash dividend, payable in two installments. The first payout of P7.08 per share is scheduled for 22 April 2026 to shareholders on record 08 April 2026.
GT Capital President Carmelo Maria Luza Bautista said the results reflect the group’s “strength amid a complex political and economic landscape.”
He added that core businesses “remained fundamentally sound, demonstrating sustained demand and operational discipline,” and said the company is “well-positioned to deliver long-term value.”
Metrobank posted net income of P49.7 billion. Pre-provision operating profit rose 17.1 percent to P78.4 billion, supported by steady asset growth, resilient margins, and trading income.
President Fabian Dee said the results “reflect client trust, employee dedication, and disciplined growth,” adding the bank continues “to strengthen our balance sheet while supporting businesses and consumers that drive the Philippine economy.”
Key metrics included net interest income of P124.6 billion, gross loans up 8.8 percent, and non-interest income of P33.5 billion, up 11.6 percent. Operating costs grew 3.3 percent, keeping the cost-to-income ratio at 50.7 percent.
Non-performing loans remained at 1.7 percent, with coverage of 140.8 percent. Total assets reached P3.9 trillion, up 10.2 percent. Capital ratios were reported at CAR 16.8 percent and CET1 16.1 percent.
Toyota Motor Philippines (TMP) reported net income of P19.0 billion, up 18.9 percent, supported by a 5.2 percent increase in retail sales to 229,447 units, led by the Vios and Avanza.
The company captured 46.7 percent market share, securing its 24th consecutive Triple Crown in passenger car, commercial vehicle, and overall sales.
Electrified vehicles accounted for 8.5 percent of sales, up from 0.33 percent in 2020, led by the Zenix, Yaris Cross, and Corolla Cross. TMP also launched the Toyota ATIV, its most accessible hybrid, and the bz4X, its first full battery-electric vehicle in the Philippines.
President Masando Hashimoto said the company’s “multi-pathway approach continues to deliver mobility solutions amid evolving fuel challenges.”
Federal Land posted net income of P522.3 million. Projects include The Season’s Residences, Grand Hyatt, and The Estate Makati, a Norman Foster-designed joint venture with SMDC, set for early 2027 completion.
Five towers were completed and handed over across Manila, Pasig, Marikina, Pasay, and Taguig.
Federal Land’s joint venture with Nomura Real Estate, FNG, sold out its first phase of Riverpark North commercial lots and advanced the UNIQLO Logistics Facility, slated to start operations in the first half of 2026.
MPIC reported consolidated core net income of P27.1 billion, up 15 percent. Contributions from operations rose 13 percent to P32.1 billion, led by Meralco power generation, Maynilad Water tariffs, and higher hospital patient volumes.
Power contributed 69 percent of net operating income, while Water and Toll Roads added 42 percent combined. Reported net income totaled P29.7 billion, tempered by a prior-year one-time gain.
AXA Philippines grew net income to P2.5 billion, with life premiums up 20 percent to P5.2 billion. Non-life gross written premiums rose 24 percent to P4.2 billion, supported by Motor CLG programs, unit-linked products, and corporate solutions.

label: koreatimes.co.kr;Gov't expands fuel tax cut in preparation for looming energy crisis;https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/politics/20260326/govt-expands-fuel-tax-cut-in-preparation-for-looming-energy-crisis;2026-03-26T07:32:00+00:00
text:
Korea will expand fuel tax cuts — from 7 percent to 15 percent for gasoline and from 10 percent to 25 percent for diesel — to ease financial pressure on drivers and industries as oil supply disruptions are expected to continue amid the Middle East conflict.
The government is also seeking to secure alternative liquefied natural gas (LNG) suppliers, amid reports that Qatar declared force majeure on its contracts with several countries including Korea.
The government announced a set of emergency measures in a meeting at Cheong Wa Dae to review the impact of the Middle East conflict on Korea’s economy, as the volatility in international oil prices and financial markets has increased significantly.
It decided to extend the tax cut policy to run until May rather than April, and also to expand the reduction rates. Under the measure, the fuel tax will decrease by 65 won ($0.04) per liter for gasoline, from 763 won to 698 won, and by 87 won for diesel, from 523 won to 436 won.
“International oil prices have risen significantly … and because such prices place too much burden on the public, we are also revising fuel taxes,” Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance and Economy Koo Yun-cheol said during a press briefing after the meeting.
President Lee Jae Myung presided over the cross-ministerial meeting, which was attended by top Cheong Wa Dae secretaries and ministers, primarily those responsible for finance, budget, commerce and other economic security-related duties.
They discussed measures to secure supply routes, conserve energy, stabilize prices and protect the people's livelihoods, as the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran has persisted for nearly a month and heightened global energy risks.
The government plans to secure LNG, including through spot purchases and LNG swaps, following an agreement already signed on March 14 between Korea Gas Corp. and Japanese energy company JERA.
The alternative supply is being arranged in response to reports that Qatar’s state-owned energy company, QatarEnergy, has declared force majeure, signaling a temporary suspension of contractual obligations due to uncontrollable events, although the Korean government said it has not received an official notification from the Qatari side.
A cross-agency crisis management headquarters, led by the deputy prime minister, will monitor supply and demand and address corporate challenges related to naphtha and other Middle East-dependent petroleum products.
A new price cap on refined petroleum products is set to take effect Friday, following the previous cap of 1,724 won per liter for gasoline, 1,713 won for diesel and 1,320 won for kerosene, which had been in place since March 13.
A hoarding ban will take effect Friday, with crackdowns on illegal or unfair practices, to stabilize the distribution of urea and diesel exhaust fluid.
About 20 items, such as manufactured goods and processed foods, affected by the Iran conflict will be designated as special management items, and the government will monitor their prices.
A supplementary budget worth 25 trillion won ($16.59 billion) is also planned.
Meanwhile, the president called for active public participation to overcome the crisis.
Lee said the government has established a broad framework to respond to the crisis, but its success will depend on the full implementation of energy-saving measures, which will rely heavily on painstaking cooperation by the people.
“This crisis is not confined to a single country ... While there is no immediate solution to turn the situation around, it is precisely at times like this that we need solidarity — pooling our wisdom and sharing the burden — more than ever,” Lee said.
“The focus now is on ensuring the measures are fully and effectively implemented,” Lee said, urging the government to “prepare in advance without overlooking even minor details” and calling on the public to “actively participate through small everyday actions.”
Additionally, he underlined a zero-tolerance policy against profiteering on high oil prices and stressed the need to conserve electricity more than ever. He noted that prices will be frozen to ease the public’s burden, but this in turn will aggravate the deficit of the already loss-making state-run Korea Electric Power Corp.
“A crisis is a true test that reveals the government’s capabilities without any embellishment. At the same time, it is also an opportunity for the government to demonstrate its ability to turn crisis into opportunity,” he said.

Looking ahead, the Tiegba Gold project in southern Côte d&CloseCurlyQuoteIvoire, acquired last year, will also be included in the valuation. Desert Gold estimates a potential of several million ounces of gold here, although no drilling has ever been conducted at this site.
But back to the current plans. The initial plans in the preliminary economic assessment called for the commissioning of a more complex CIL (carbon-in-leach) plant. Now the company is starting with a simpler process. A gravity plant, which, according to metallurgical tests, achieves a recovery rate of 68%, is set to mark the start of the production phase. Gold is described as inversely correlated with the US Dollar and US Treasuries, and also with risk assets such as equities. Gold price movements are linked to factors including geopolitical instability, recession concerns, interest rates, and US Dollar strength because gold is priced in dollars (XAU/USD).
Given the slight increase in gold prices, we should focus on the underlying factors that support the precious metal as a safe-haven asset. Last year, in 2025, we saw global economic growth slow more than anticipated, and early 2026 data suggests this trend is continuing. This environment, coupled with persistent inflation that averaged over 3.5% in the US during the final quarter of 2025, strengthens the case for holding gold as a hedge.
Key Drivers To Watch

Following the record-breaking purchases of the early 2020s, central banks collectively added another 980 tonnes to their reserves in 2025, with the People’s Bank of China and the Reserve Bank of India leading the buying. This institutional demand suggests that any significant price dips will likely be met with strong buying interest.
The inverse relationship with the US Dollar is critical for our strategy in the coming weeks. The dollar has weakened by about 2% against a basket of currencies since the start of March 2026, creating a direct tailwind for gold priced in USD. As we monitor the Federal Reserve’s language for any hints of a more dovish stance, this dollar weakness could accelerate.
For derivative traders, this environment of conflicting signals—high interest rates versus slowing growth—suggests an increase in volatility. Consider using options strategies like straddles to play a potential sharp price move, regardless of direction, as geopolitical tensions in the South China Sea continue to simmer. For those with a bullish outlook, buying call options on gold futures offers leveraged exposure while defining risk.
However, we must remain cautious about the impact of high interest rates, which typically act as a headwind for a non-yielding asset like gold. While the market has priced in the current rate environment, any indication from central banks that rates will stay higher for longer than expected could cap the upside. Therefore, using strategies like bull call spreads could be prudent to limit premium costs and define profit potential in a potentially range-bound market.

label: financefeeds.com;Binance XAUT Hits Record $6.4 Billion Volume as Tokenized Gold Trading Surges - FinanceFeeds;https://financefeeds.com/binance-xaut-hits-record-6-4-billion-volume-as-tokenized-gold-trading-surges/;2026-03-26T07:29:00+00:00
text:
Binance’s Tether Gold (XAUT) perpetual futures contract recorded a new all-time high daily trading volume of approximately $6.4 billion, marking a significant milestone for tokenized commodity trading within the crypto derivatives market. The surge underscores accelerating demand for real-world asset exposure on blockchain-based trading platforms.
The record was reached on March 23, representing a sharp increase from the $1 billion to $2 billion daily range observed earlier in the year. The rapid expansion in trading activity positions XAUT among the most actively traded perpetual contracts on Binance, reflecting a shift in market structure toward non-crypto assets.
The growth trajectory has been particularly notable given that XAUT volumes were relatively limited just months earlier, indicating a rapid increase in participation and liquidity. The contract’s rise highlights how quickly tokenized commodities are gaining traction alongside traditional crypto derivatives.
Commodities gain traction in crypto derivatives
The surge in XAUT volume reflects broader momentum in tokenized commodities, as traders increasingly seek exposure to traditional assets such as gold through crypto-native infrastructure. XAUT, issued by Tether, is backed by physical gold and allows traders to gain price exposure through perpetual futures without directly holding the underlying asset.
Market participants have pointed to macroeconomic uncertainty, inflation expectations, and volatility in traditional financial markets as key drivers behind increased demand for gold-linked trading. Elevated activity suggests both speculative positioning and hedging demand.
The rise in XAUT also aligns with a broader trend of commodities gaining prominence within crypto derivatives markets. Tokenized assets such as gold, oil, and silver are increasingly traded alongside Bitcoin and Ethereum, signaling a shift in capital allocation strategies among market participants.
Binance’s infrastructure has supported this growth by enabling 24/7 trading, leveraged exposure, and stablecoin-settled contracts. Continuous market access allows traders to respond to global developments in real time, particularly during periods when traditional commodity markets are closed.
RWA expansion reshapes market structure
The record volume in XAUT highlights a structural evolution in crypto markets, where centralized and decentralized exchanges are integrating real-world financial instruments into digital trading environments. The growing popularity of tokenized gold suggests that blockchain-based platforms are becoming viable venues for macro positioning.
The development also aligns with broader efforts by exchanges to expand into cross-asset trading. Increasing availability of tokenized commodities and equities is contributing to the convergence between traditional finance and digital asset markets.
For market participants, the surge in XAUT trading indicates a shift toward diversification beyond crypto-native volatility. Traders are increasingly using tokenized commodities to hedge risk, express macroeconomic views, and access traditional markets through a unified trading infrastructure.
At the same time, the rapid growth in volume raises considerations around market structure and oversight. As trading in tokenized real-world assets scales, regulatory attention and infrastructure requirements are expected to increase.
The $6.4 billion daily volume milestone positions XAUT as one of the fastest-growing derivatives products in the crypto ecosystem. The trend underscores the expanding role of tokenized commodities in digital asset markets and points to continued integration between blockchain-based trading platforms and traditional financial instruments.

2025 Financial Year
2025 Figures: KSB Outperforms Previous Year
Growth in order intake, sales revenue and earnings EBIT increased to € 252.1 million and margin to 8.3 % Dividend proposal of € 26.50 per ordinary share
FRANKENTHAL: Pump and valve manufacturer KSB continues its path of growth: In the 2025 financial year, the company passed the € 3 billion mark in both order intake and, for the first time, sales revenue. The SDAX-listed Group also increased its EBIT (earnings before finance income / expense and income tax).
In the 2025 financial year, KSB increased order intake by 2.9 % to € 3,203 million. Adjusted for currency translation effects, order intake would have increased by 5.6 %. The Pumps Segment reported the strongest growth of 6.1 % to € 1,760 million, which was driven, in particular, by the Water Market, which grew by 12.5 %. The Valves Segment reported order intake of € 413 million, a year-on-year increase of 1.4 %. In the KSB SupremeServ Segment, which covers business with spare parts and service, order intake declined by 1.7 % to € 1,031 million. Reasons for this were currency translation effects and lower demand for spare parts from the Mining and Energy Markets.
Sales revenue at KSB exceeded the € 3 billion mark for the first time in the 2025 financial year, increasing by 2.3 % to € 3,035 million. Adjusted for currency translation effects, sales revenue would have been up 5.0 %. The Pumps Segment reported the highest growth, increasing by 4.3 % to € 1,618 million. The Valves Segment reported sales revenue of € 404 million, a rise of 1.3 %. At € 1,013 million, sales revenue in the KSB SupremeServ Segment remained at around the previous year’s level. It was impacted by both currency translation effects and a 5 % decline in sales revenue in the Mining Market. In all other Markets, sales revenue remained stable or slightly above the prior-year level, adjusted for currency translation effects.

Spot Gold's Sharp Recovery from Monthly Lows
The current spot gold price stands at $4,636.60 per ounce, marking a daily gain of $21.96 or 0.47%, according to live market data timestamped 12:32 AM ET on March 26. This level represents a significant snapback from intraday lows near $4,100 earlier in the week, amid one of the most turbulent periods for the gold market in recent memory. The rebound follows a broader monthly correction where spot gold shed nearly 10% from January peaks above $5,500, driven initially by heightened geopolitical risks from the US-Iran war but later by unwinding momentum trades.
U.S. investors tracking COMEX gold futures will note that front-month contracts have mirrored this spot recovery, though futures remain sensitive to New York session positioning. The distinction matters: spot gold reflects over-the-counter physical trading, while COMEX futures incorporate leveraged speculative flows, which amplified the recent downside volatility. As of the latest available data, no official LBMA Gold Price benchmark has been published for March 26, but prior auctions provide context for institutional pricing benchmarks.
Key Drivers: Weaker Dollar and Easing Oil Pressures
A softening U.S. dollar has been the primary catalyst for gold's uptick, reversing some of the currency's strength that pressured prices earlier in March. Gold, priced in dollars, becomes more affordable for international buyers when the greenback weakens, boosting physical and ETF demand. This dynamic is particularly relevant for U.S. investors holding dollar-denominated assets, as dollar depreciation enhances gold's relative value in diversified portfolios.
Easing crude oil prices have also contributed, slipping despite year-on-year gains fueled by the Iran conflict. Lower oil reduces inflationary expectations, indirectly supporting gold by curbing aggressive Federal Reserve rate hike bets. The 10-year Treasury yield, recently at 4.384%, has shown signs of stabilization, lowering the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold compared to bonds. For American investors, this interplay highlights gold's role as a hedge against both inflation and currency risks.
US-Iran Tensions: From Rally to Correction
The gold price surge in early 2026 was propelled by escalating US-Iran hostilities, drawing safe-haven flows into bullion and precious metals. Silver and gold both posted year-on-year gains, with gold maintaining positive monthly returns for 36 consecutive months until the recent pullback. However, as diplomatic signals emerged—described in market commentary as 'cautious'—investors shifted from panic buying to profit-taking, exacerbating the 14% drop from January's all-time high of $5,594.92.
This pattern is familiar in geopolitical-driven gold moves: initial spikes give way to tactical corrections as risk sentiment normalizes. U.S. investors should monitor official statements from Washington and Tehran, as any confirmed de-escalation could cap near-term upside, while renewed flare-ups would likely propel spot gold toward $4,800 resistance levels.
Market Structure and ETF Implications for U.S. Investors
COMEX futures positioning reveals overcrowded longs unwinding, a classic driver of sharp corrections in commodities. Retail and systematic funds, which piled in during the 2025 bull run, have been net sellers, adding downward pressure. For U.S. investors, this translates to opportunities in physically backed ETFs like GLD or IAU, where inflows could accelerate if spot gold sustains above $4,600.

De-dollarization trends among emerging markets further bolster the long-term case, even as short-term volatility persists. Major institutions such as J.P. Morgan ($6,300 target) and Deutsche Bank ($6,000) view the dip as tactical, not structural.

Volatility metrics indicate the most turbulent March in decades, with daily swings exceeding 3-5%. Risks and Counterpoints for Balanced Positioning
While the rebound is encouraging, risks abound. A stronger dollar rebound or hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data could reverse gains swiftly. Fed expectations for rate cuts have dimmed amid fiscal concerns, elevating yields and opportunity costs. Geopolitical wildcards, including Iran-related oil disruptions, add uncertainty—crude's year-on-year rise after 20 months underscores energy-gold linkages.

DAX Index Climbs 1.41% to 22,957 Amid Geopolitical Resilience and Positive German Ifo Data
26.03.2026 - 08:46:02 | ad-hoc-news.deThe DAX index, Germany's benchmark equity gauge tracking 40 major companies, posted a robust 1.41% advance to finish at 22,957.08 points on March 25, 2026. This recovery came after an early dip on March 24, highlighting market resilience amid escalating geopolitical risks in the Middle East.
As of: Thursday, March 26, 2026, 8:45 Europe/Berlin (converted from 7:45 UTC)
Geopolitical Backdrop and Market Snapback
Despite Iran's rejection of a partial ceasefire proposal and calls for a full halt to hostilities, European stocks including the DAX pushed higher. The index's climb reflects investor confidence in de-escalation potential, even as USD strength pressured the euro. This move separated the DAX cash index from premarket jitters, with DE40 futures briefly topping 23,200 points intraday.
The DAX outperformed its early session weakness on March 24, where it fell 0.8%, underscoring quick snapback dynamics typical of cyclical-heavy benchmarks. German exporters, a core DAX driver, benefited from a weaker euro at 1.158 versus the USD, easing competitiveness concerns.
Ifo Business Climate Boosts Sentiment
Germany's Ifo business climate index registered 86.4 in March, edging above consensus forecasts of 86.2, though off the prior 86.7 reading. This upside surprise acted as a direct catalyst for DAX cyclicals, signaling stabilizing confidence among manufacturers and services firms central to the index's composition.
The reading underscores resilience in Germany's industrial base, with implications for DAX heavyweights in autos, chemicals, and machinery. Positive Ifo data often transmits to the index via improved earnings outlooks for export-oriented firms, countering broader Eurozone headwinds.
DAX Cash vs. Futures Divergence
While the DAX cash index settled at 22,957.08 after a 1.41% rise, Eurex DE40 futures traded above 23,200 during the session, pointing to overnight optimism. Investors distinguish these: cash reflects 40 blue-chips' closing prices, while futures incorporate global cues like U.S. futures and Asian handoff.
This futures premium suggests positioning for continued upside, potentially fueled by ECB rate cut bets. DAX futures volume remains key for liquidity assessment, separate from spot ETF flows.
Sector Rotation and Key Constituents
Autos and industrials led DAX gains, with sector rotation favoring cyclicals over defensives. This aligns with Ifo's manufacturing stabilization, benefiting names like Volkswagen and Siemens in the 40-stock universe. No single constituent dominated; broad participation drove the index-level move.
Chemicals and basic materials also contributed, as Bund yields stabilized amid ECB watchful eyes. The DAX's export sensitivity amplified these shifts, distinct from less trade-exposed peers like the FTSE 100.
European Peers and U.S. Context
The DAX's 1.41% gain outpaced the CAC 40's 1.33% and FTSE's similar rise, with Poland's WIG20 leading at over 2%. This relative strength highlights Germany's macro edge via Ifo data. Versus the S&P 500, the DAX showed parallel risk-on, but euro weakness added a currency overlay for U.S. investors.
UK CPI at 3.2% year-on-year, above 3.1% expected, had muted Euro impact, as ECB focus dominates DAX pricing.
ECB Expectations and Bund Yields
DAX moves tie closely to ECB policy bets, with markets pricing June rate cuts amid sticky inflation. Stable Bund yields supported financials within the index, while a softer euro aided exporters. Upcoming Eurozone PMIs will test this dynamic.
Geopolitical risks linger, but DAX positioning reflects a base case of ECB easing outweighing Middle East tensions.
ETF and Derivatives Implications
DAX-linked ETFs saw inflows on the rebound, mirroring cash upside. Products like those tracking DE0008469008 benefit directly from index gains. Options activity likely built gamma at 23,000 strike, per futures flows.
For international investors, this episode reinforces DAX's role as a pure Euro cyclical play, with U.S. dollar strength offering hedging tailwinds.
Risks and Next Catalysts
Upside risks include further Ifo rebound or ECB dovishness; downsides from Iran escalation or U.S. tariff rhetoric. Watch March 28 PMIs and Q1 earnings for DAX direction.
Historical context: From March 24 close at 22,852.66, the 1.13% March 25 open led to full recovery, building on March 26's 22,839.03 session.

New Delhi, March 26 : India's health insurance sector has recorded strong growth, with total premiums crossing Rs 1.2 lakh crore in 2024-25, the government said on Thursday.
New Delhi, March 26 (IANS) IndiaĂ˘â‚¬â„˘s health insurance sector has recorded strong growth, with total premiums crossing Rs 1.2 lakh crore in 2024-25, the government said on Thursday.
IndiaĂ˘â‚¬â„˘s health insurance sector continues to expand steadily, growing at around 9 per cent annually, driven by increasing awareness, better access to healthcare financing and a rising need for financial protection against medical expenses.
To improve efficiency and ensure faster support to policyholders, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India has set strict timelines for processing cashless health insurance claims.
As per the norms, insurers must approve cashless pre-authorisation requests within one hour, while final approval must be completed within three hours.
These measures are aimed at reducing delays and ensuring patients get timely treatment, the government stated.
The rise in health insurance premiums has been attributed to multiple factors, including ageing policyholders, higher coverage amounts and improved policy features.
The regulatorĂ˘â‚¬â„˘s 2024 guidelines also ensure that insurance products are priced fairly based on risk factors, with regular reviews using data and customer feedback.
In terms of claims settlement, the sector has shown improvement. The claims paid ratio stood at 87.5 per cent in 2024-25, compared to 82.46 per cent in 2023-24 and 85.66 per cent in 2022-23.
Data from the IRDAIĂ˘â‚¬â„˘s Bima Bharosa portal shows that 1,37,361 grievances related to general and health insurance were reported in FY25.
Of these, about 93 per cent were resolved within the same financial year, it added.
However, some claims continue to be rejected due to policy-related conditions such as exceeding the sum insured, co-payment clauses, sub-limits, deductibles, room rent caps and non-medical expenses.
The regulator has taken several steps to improve transparency and streamline the claims process.
These efforts are aimed at building greater trust among policyholders and ensuring a more efficient and reliable health insurance system in the country.

US-Iran Ceasefire Talks Boost Wall Street Optimism Amid Geopolitical Tensions
26.03.2026 - 08:59:46 | ad-hoc-news.deU.S. investors saw a welcome relief rally on Wall Street Tuesday as prospects of a US-Iran ceasefire emerged, driving major indices higher despite lingering geopolitical clouds. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average closed with gains, reflecting optimism that de-escalation in the Middle East could ease oil price pressures and support consumer spending amid high inflation concerns.
As of: Thursday, March 26, 2026, 3:59 AM ET
Wall Street's Reaction to Ceasefire Signals
The buzz around US-Iran truce talks dominated market chatter late Tuesday, with Bloomberg Surveillance noting how Asian stocks weighed the developments early Wednesday Asia time, but U.S. markets had already priced in the positive tilt by the close. The Dow climbed 0.8%, the S&P 500 added 1.1%, and Nasdaq rose 1.4%, led by tech and consumer discretionary names betting on lower energy costs. For U.S. retail and professional investors, this shift matters because sustained high oil prices have been a drag on everything from airline stocks to grocery bills, potentially influencing Fed rate cut expectations.
Energy sector stocks bucked the trend, sliding 1.2% as crude futures eased on de-escalation hopes. ExxonMobil and Chevron dipped, but defense contractors like Lockheed Martin and Raytheon surged over 3%, as traders rotated into safe-haven plays should talks falter. This dynamic underscores a key portfolio strategy for Americans: balancing energy exposure with defense hedges in volatile times.
Geopolitical Context Driving the Move
Reports of wrangling between the U.S. and Iran over ceasefire terms surfaced amid conflicting signals from the region, sapping some sentiment but ultimately lifting stocks on truce prospects. Bloomberg's Horizons Middle East & Africa segment highlighted how oil gained initially on tensions but pared back as diplomatic channels opened. For U.S. investors, the stakes are high: prolonged conflict could spike Brent crude above $100 per barrel, hammering S&P 500 earnings by 5-7% via higher input costs, per analyst models.
The timing aligns with broader market fatigue from Fed tightening. With the federal funds rate at 5.25-5.50%, any oil relief bolsters the case for cuts later this year, boosting rate-sensitive sectors like real estate and utilities. Professional investors are eyeing VIX futures, which dropped to 18, signaling calming volatility bets.
Implications for Key U.S. Sectors
Consumer staples and discretionary stocks led gains, with Procter & Gamble up 1.5% and Amazon rising 2.2%, as lower oil forecasts improve margins. Airlines like Delta and United soared 4%, recouping losses from prior tension spikes. This rotation favors diversified U.S. equity portfolios, particularly those heavy in cyclicals.
Conversely, the energy rout hit smaller producers hardest, with Occidental Petroleum down 2.5%. Yet, supermajors remain resilient due to global demand. U.S. Treasuries saw yields dip slightly, with the 10-year at 4.15%, as safe-haven flows reversed. For bond investors, this ceasefire hope tempers inflation fears tied to energy, potentially steepening the yield curve favorably.
Investor Strategies in Uncertain Times
Retail traders on platforms like Robinhood piled into defense ETFs such as ITA, which jumped 2.8%. Professional funds adjusted overweight positions in energy to neutral, per 13F insights. A prudent approach for U.S. investors: maintain 5-10% in commodities via USO or DBC for hedges, while overweighting quality cyclicals like those in the S&P 500 Equal Weight Index.
Risk management is key. If talks collapse, oil could rebound sharply, benefiting XLE holders but pressuring broader indices. Options volume spiked in energy puts, indicating savvy bets on volatility crush. Dollar strength eased slightly versus euro, supporting multinational earnings translation for Dow components.
Broadening Market Context
Beyond Iran, SpaceX IPO speculation added tailwinds, with whispers of it becoming America's largest ever, drawing parallels to defense tech synergies. Trump-Xi meeting rumors for May in Beijing provided counterbalance, potentially easing trade frictions impacting U.S. semis and industrials.
U.S. economic data remains supportive: Tuesday's consumer confidence beat estimates at 105.2, reinforcing soft-landing narratives. ISM manufacturing PMI held at 48.5, signaling stabilization. These factors amplify the ceasefire's positive skew for 2026 equity outlooks.
Risks and What to Watch Next
Key risks include negotiation breakdowns, with Iranian hardliners reportedly resistant. Oil inventories data due Wednesday could confirm supply dynamics. Fed Chair Powell's upcoming testimony will gauge inflation-oil linkages. Investors should monitor EIA reports and Middle East headlines closely.
For long-term positioning, consider dividend aristocrats in consumer sectors for yield amid volatility. ESG funds face headwinds if defense outperforms, prompting allocation reviews. Overall, the truce prospects tilt risk-reward favorably for U.S. bullish bias.
Global Ripples and U.S. Dollar Impact
Asian markets extended gains early Wednesday, with Nikkei up 1.2%, correlating to Wall Street's close. European bourses like DAX rose 0.9%, but U.S. investors focus on domestic spillovers. The dollar index slipped to 104.2, aiding exporters like Caterpillar and Boeing.
Commodity plays extend to gold, which pared gains to $2,650/oz as risk appetite returned. Crypto markets, Bitcoin at $95,000, mirrored equities on de-risking. U.S.-listed Bitcoin ETFs saw inflows, blending traditional and alt assets.
Technical Outlook for Major Indices
S&P 500 broke above 5,800 resistance, eyeing 6,000. RSI at 62 suggests room to run without overbought. Dow targets 42,500, supported by financials. Nasdaq's tech leadership, with NVDA up 3%, points to AI momentum persisting.
Volatility surfaces remain cheap; consider VIX calls for protection. Sector rotation favors industrials over energy, per relative strength indicators.
Portfolio Adjustments for Retail Investors
Robinhood users boosted positions in SPY and QQQ. Vanguard's VTI saw record volumes. Advice: diversify via target-date funds, allocating 60% equities, 30% bonds, 10% alts. Rebalance quarterly to capture rotations.
Tax implications: harvest losses in energy for offsets. 401(k) contributions to growth funds capitalize on momentum.
Professional Insights and Analyst Views
Goldman Sachs raised S&P targets to 6,100, citing geopolitical thaw. JPMorgan warns of oil rebound risks. Consensus EPS growth at 12% for 2026 supports multiples expansion.

label: watcher.guru;JP Morgan Updates Gold Target Price: Gains Now & End of 2026 Prediction;https://watcher.guru/news/jp-morgan-updates-gold-target-price-gains-now-end-of-2026-prediction;2026-03-26T08:04:00+00:00
text:
The gold target price JP Morgan set for year-end 2026 is $6,300 per ounce, and the bank reaffirmed that figure on February 25, the same day it raised its short-term forecast by 15% to $4,500 an ounce. Central bank gold buying, U.S. Treasury divestment announcements, and a shift in reserve preferences away from the dollar all fed into that decision. The gold target price today already shows those forces at work: spot gold has climbed around 20% in 2026 so far, after a 64% surge through 2025. For anyone thinking about gold portfolio allocation right now, the numbers are hard to miss.
Also Read: Gold Hits 4-Month Low as Rates Spike: $400 Rebound & $10K Target
Gold Target 2026 Insights From JP Morgan On Investor And Bank Trends
JP Morgan’s Revised Numbers
The gold target price JP Morgan originally penciled in for year-end 2026 was around $5,000 per ounce. Gold ran through that months ahead of schedule, hitting an all-time high of $5,594.82 on January 29. The February 25 note kept the $6,300 year-end target in place and also pushed the long-term gold target price JP Morgan now works with up to $4,500 — the bank assigned more weight to what it calls a “reserve currency paradigm shift” and to a structural, ongoing diversification by both investors and central banks into gold.
Natasha Kaneva, Head of Global Commodities Strategy at J.P. Morgan, stated:
“While this rally in gold has not, and will not, be linear, we believe the trends driving this rebasing higher in gold prices are not exhausted. The long-term trend of official reserve and investor diversification into gold has further to run.”
Central Banks Are Still in the Market
JP Morgan projects central bank gold buying will total around 755 tonnes in 2026. That sits below the 1,000-plus tonne annual pace of the last three years, but it also still runs well above the 400–500 tonne pre-2022 average — and it forms a big part of why the gold target price JP Morgan revised upward again in February. The slowdown is largely mechanical: at prices above $4,000 an ounce, central banks simply don’t need to buy as many tonnes to hit their target allocation.
Globally, central bank gold holdings now stand at nearly 36,200 tonnes and account for close to 20% of official reserves, up from around 15% at the end of 2023, per IMF data. The gold target price JP Morgan tracks connects directly to this demand floor — and without sustained central bank gold buying, the $6,300 year-end target gets a lot harder to defend.
Gregory Shearer, Head of Base and Precious Metals Strategy at J.P. Morgan, stated:
“We believe central bank demand will remain elevated next year and have been encouraged by strong buying in the third quarter of 2025, even with much higher gold prices.”
Gold Portfolio Allocation: How Much Is Enough?
Gold portfolio allocation across ETFs, physical bars and coins, and COMEX futures sat at around 2.8% of total investor AUM as of late 2025. JP Morgan sees that climbing toward 4–5% over the coming years, with around 250 tonnes of ETF inflows and also over 1,200 tonnes of bar and coin demand expected in 2026 alone. The bank also flagged a scenario where redirecting just 0.5% of foreign U.S. asset holdings into gold would push the gold target 2026 figure all the way to $6,000 per ounce on its own. If that plays out, even the gold target price JP Morgan currently publishes would look like it’s undershooting the mark.
Shearer added:
“While gold’s share of total investor AUM has grown by around one percentage point over the last two years as prices and demand have increased, we still see the potential for this share to rise toward 4–5% over the coming years.”
Jonathan Steinberg, founder and CEO of WisdomTree, stated in a March 24 interview with Barron’s:
“If you go back to Jack Bogle, the founder of Vanguard, and his approach to investing: own the world of liquid assets proportionally to their market cap. Under that scenario, gold would be about 12% of your portfolio.”
Broader Analyst Consensus
The broader analyst consensus aligns with the gold target price JP Morgan has published. Wells Fargo sits at $6,100–$6,300 by year-end, UBS at $6,200, Deutsche Bank at $6,000, and Société Générale also at $6,000. Central bank gold buying shows no sign of slowing, gold portfolio allocation keeps growing across both retail and institutional investors, and the gold target price today continues to move higher. The 2026 forecasts that felt aggressive a few months ago now look, if anything, conservative — and the gold target price JP Morgan is working with could yet move up again.

For nearly four weeks, the conflict between Iran and Israel – and the potential for wider regional escalation – had injected significant volatility into global markets. The prospect of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire, even one contingent on complex negotiations, is enough to trigger a ‘risk-on’ sentiment. However, the situation remains fluid. Decoding the Market Response: Beyond the Headlines
The gains across major European indices – FTSE 100 (+1.4%), CAC 40 (+1.3%), and DAX (+1.4%) – indicate broad-based investor optimism. But the underlying drivers are nuanced. The decline in oil prices directly benefits European economies heavily reliant on imported energy. However, the threat of further escalation remains a significant overhang. Iranians officials, including Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, have signaled a reluctance to engage in negotiations while hostilities continue. This creates a fundamental disconnect between market hopes and political realities.
The Iran Threat: A Deeper Look at Potential Disruptions
The reported threat by an unnamed Iranian official to target ships in the Red Sea introduces a new dimension of risk. This could disrupt global trade routes, particularly those vital for energy and manufactured goods. The Wall Street Journal highlights the potential for increased insurance costs and shipping delays, which would exacerbate inflationary pressures. What we have is where the market’s optimism may be misplaced. While a full-scale ground invasion by the U.S. Appears unlikely, even limited disruptions to Red Sea shipping could have significant economic consequences.
Currency Movements and the Dollar’s Role
The weakening of the Euro and British Pound against the dollar reflects a flight to safety, albeit a muted one. The dollar traditionally benefits from periods of geopolitical uncertainty, as investors seek its perceived stability. However, the magnitude of the currency movements was relatively tiny, suggesting that the market does not anticipate a major escalation. The dollar’s rise against the Japanese Yen, however, is more pronounced, indicating a stronger risk-off sentiment among Japanese investors. But the balance sheet tells a different story, the yen’s weakness also reflects the Bank of Japan’s continued ultra-loose monetary policy.

label: dailynews.co.tz;Services receipts drive up Z'bar current account surplus;https://dailynews.co.tz/services-receipts-drive-up-zbar-current-account-surplus/;2026-03-26T06:44:00+00:00
text:
ZANZIBAR: THE Zanzibar current account surplus has rose by 25.8 per cent to 896.6 million US dollars in the year ending January, up from the corresponding period last year, largely driven by increased services receipts.
According to the latest Bank of Tanzania Monthly Economic Review, the growth was primarily supported by a stronger performance in tourism-related activities, indicating a sustained recovery in the services sector and its growing contribution to external sector stability.
Exports of goods and services grew by 26.9 per cent to 1.63 billion US dollars in the year ending January, compared with the corresponding period last year, signalling a notable strengthening in external demand.
The increase suggests improved competitiveness and higher earnings from both traditional and non-traditional exports, reinforcing the external sector’s role in supporting overall economic growth and foreign exchange inflows.
Services receipts remained the dominant component of exports of goods and services, accounting for about 94 per cent of total earnings.
This strong contribution was largely underpinned by a rise in international tourist arrivals to 933,314, up from 747,356 in the corresponding period last year, highlighting the sector’s central role in driving export growth and foreign exchange inflows.
The increase in goods exports was mainly attributable to a rise of traditional exports, notably cloves, reflecting seasonal and cyclical nature of crop production.
On a month-on-month comparative basis, exports of goods and services rose to 173.6 million US dollars in January, up from 141 million US dollars recorded in January last year.
ALSO READ: Z’bar current account surplus widens on tourism
This increase points to a sustained improvement in external demand and export performance, reinforcing the upward trajectory observed in the broader annual trend.
Imports of goods and services increased by 27.8 per cent to 757.9 million US dollars in the year ending January, compared with the corresponding period last year.
The expansion was largely driven by higher imports of capital and consumer goods, suggesting strengthening domestic demand and ongoing investment activity, with potential implications for future productive capacity and economic growth.
Imports of capital goods surged by 89.4 per cent to 116.3 million US dollars primarily driven by increased purchases of industrial transport equipment.
This sharp rise points to intensified investment in productive infrastructure and logistics capacity signalling efforts to enhance industrial efficiency and support medium-to longterm economic growth.
Meanwhile, the increase in imports of consumer goods was mainly attributed to elevated purchases of non-industrial transport equipment and other consumer goods, including insecticides, rodenticides and related products.
On a month-on-month comparative basis, imports of goods and services rose to 84 million US dollars in January, up from 44.7 million US dollars recorded in January last year.

label: ssbcrack.com;WNBA Ratifies New Collective Bargaining Agreement, Signaling Historic Salary Increases for Players -;https://news.ssbcrack.com/wnba-ratifies-new-collective-bargaining-agreement-signaling-historic-salary-increases-for-players/;2026-03-26T08:09:00+00:00
text:
In a significant move towards player empowerment and fair compensation, the WNBA has announced a historic collective bargaining agreement (CBA) that will dramatically increase salaries for players beginning in the 2026 season. The league’s board of governors ratified the new seven-year deal unanimously, shortly after the players’ approval, bringing a slew of changes aimed at elevating the status and financial wellbeing of athletes within the league.
The forthcoming season will see a substantial increase in the salary cap, soaring from $1.5 million in 2025 to an impressive $7 million per team in 2026. This shift underscores the league’s commitment to providing players with more substantial financial packages, a key element that has been at the forefront of negotiations.
One of the most notable examples of the incoming salary structure can be observed in elite veteran contracts. Players like A’ja Wilson, a pivotal figure for the Las Vegas Aces, stand to benefit immensely. Formerly earning $200,000, Wilson’s projected salary for the 2026 season is an astounding $1.4 million, making her eligible for a supermax deal. Known for her exceptional contributions, including a recent championship and multiple MVP awards, Wilson is poised to be a central focus for general managers eyeing championship rosters.
The 2026 CBA also defines average veteran salaries, estimated to be approximately $583,800. For instance, Alanna Smith, a respected forward with considerable experience, is projected to earn around $600,000 next season, reflecting her integral role in her team’s success in recent years.
For veteran players at the minimum salary tier, the new CBA also signals positive changes. Erica Wheeler, a seasoned guard, is expected to see her salary rise to $300,000, a notable increase from her previous earnings. Wheeler’s contributions on and off the court, especially given her leadership qualities, underscore the value of experience in the league.
The agreement additionally benefits incoming rookies, particularly for high-profile talents such as Caitlin Clark, who is projected to earn approximately $530,000 in her third year. The revised rookie contracts are structured to offer substantial pay increases while providing opportunities for renegotiation and contract extensions based on performance, further enhancing the financial landscape for new players.
As teams prepare for significant transitions, including upcoming expansion drafts for new franchises in Toronto and Portland, the WNBA is set to embark on an exciting chapter. Key dates are fast approaching; the expansion drafts will occur on April 6, followed by an extensive free agency period starting the next day, and the collegiate and overseas draft slated for April 13.
As interest in women’s basketball continues to rise, this new CBA marks a transformative moment in the WNBA, showcasing the league’s commitment to its players’ growth and stability within professional sports. The focus now shifts to how teams will leverage these changes to build competitive rosters and enhance the overall quality of the game.

label: thesun.ng;Middle East war opens LNG opportunities for Nigeria - NNPC;https://thesun.ng/middle-east-war-opens-lng-opportunities-for-nigeria-nnpc/;2026-03-26T08:03:00+00:00
text:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) says the ongoing conflict in the Middle East is creating fresh commercial opportunities for Nigeria, as global energy markets adjust to disruptions triggered by the war involving Israel, United States and Iran.
Speaking at the CERAWeek energy conference in Houston, the company’s Executive Vice President, Olalekan Ogunleye, said Nigeria is witnessing stronger demand for its liquefied natural gas as buyers seek more reliable supply routes.
“We are right in the middle of the market. We are 10 sailing days from Europe, close to the Atlantic Basin, and close to Asia,” Ogunleye said. “We see commercial opportunities on top of the fact that we have the most gas reserves in Africa.”
He explained that Nigeria LNG Limited currently exports up to 22 million metric tonnes annually and is expanding with a seventh production train expected by 2027, positioning the country to take advantage of shifting global demand.
Ogunleye added that gas demand has remained resilient despite geopolitical tensions, revealing that NNPC is already discussing plans for additional LNG trains and a 12 million metric tonnes per annum project to harness Nigeria’s vast gas reserves.
Industry observers, including LNG consultant Martin Houston, say the conflict has heightened the need for supply diversification, opening the door for African producers like Nigeria to gain a stronger foothold in the global market.
Meanwhile, Nigeria’s Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Heineken Lokpobiri, said the government is intensifying efforts to attract investors, insisting the country now offers stability, regulatory clarity and a competitive edge as global energy players reassess their priorities.

Crypto wallet users exceeded 420 million globally by the end of 2024, according to data from Statista and Crypto.com. That figure represents a 230% increase from 2020, when approximately 130 million wallet addresses were active. The growth has been driven by exchange-hosted wallets, self-custody solutions like MetaMask, and mobile wallets in emerging markets where crypto serves as a practical financial tool rather than a speculative asset.
What Is Driving Wallet Growth
Exchange-hosted wallets account for the majority of crypto users. Coinbase reported 110 million verified users by the end of 2024. Binance claims more than 200 million registered accounts globally. These platforms make wallet creation automatic when a user signs up, lowering the barrier to entry. A new user can create an account, complete identity verification, and hold crypto within minutes.
Self-custody wallets have also grown substantially. MetaMask, the most popular browser-based Ethereum wallet, reached more than 30 million monthly active users in 2024, according to Consensys. Trust Wallet, owned by Binance, reported more than 70 million users. Phantom, a Solana-focused wallet, grew from 2 million to more than 7 million users between 2022 and 2024 as Solana DeFi and NFT activity expanded.
Mobile wallets are growing fastest in emerging markets. In Nigeria, more than 35 million people use crypto, according to a 2024 survey by KuCoin. In the Philippines, GCash and Coins.ph have integrated crypto trading into their mobile payment platforms, reaching millions of users. In Argentina, where annual inflation exceeded 200% in 2024, crypto wallets like Lemon Cash and Belo attracted millions of users seeking dollar-denominated stablecoins. Fintech startups expanding across emerging markets are increasingly incorporating crypto wallet functionality.
The Role of Institutional Wallets
Institutional crypto custody has become a major segment. Coinbase Custody holds more than $170 billion in assets on behalf of institutional clients, including hedge funds, pension funds, and ETF providers. Fidelity Digital Assets, launched in 2018, custodies billions in bitcoin and ether for institutional investors. BitGo processes more than $50 billion in monthly transactions across 700 institutional clients.
The approval of spot Bitcoin ETFs in the US created massive institutional custody demand. The 11 approved ETFs collectively hold more than $100 billion in bitcoin, all stored in institutional custody wallets. Coinbase Custody is the custodian for BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust, the largest crypto ETF. This institutional layer represents a smaller number of wallets but an enormous share of total crypto value.
Multi-party computation wallets are a growing category for institutions. Fireblocks, which provides MPC-based custody, has processed more than $6 trillion in digital asset transactions since launch. MPC wallets split private keys across multiple parties, eliminating single points of failure. Fintech revenue growth in the custody segment reflects this institutional demand for secure wallet infrastructure.
Wallet Technology Is Evolving
Account abstraction, introduced through Ethereum’s ERC-4337 standard, is making wallets easier to use. Traditional crypto wallets require users to manage seed phrases and pay gas fees in ETH. Account abstraction allows wallets to implement social recovery (where friends or family can help restore access), gasless transactions (where the application pays fees), and session keys (which allow pre-approved actions without repeated confirmations).
Smart wallets built on account abstraction processed more than 10 million transactions in 2024, according to Dune Analytics. Coinbase launched Smart Wallet in June 2024, which creates a crypto wallet using just an email address or biometric login, with no seed phrase required. Safe (formerly Gnosis Safe) manages more than $100 billion in assets through its smart contract wallet, used primarily by DAOs and crypto treasuries.
Hardware wallets provide the highest security for self-custody. Ledger has sold more than 7 million hardware wallets, according to the company. Trezor has sold more than 2 million. These devices store private keys offline, protecting against online attacks. As digital banking customers approach 3.6 billion, crypto wallets are becoming part of the broader digital financial toolkit.
What 420 Million Wallets Means for the Industry
The 420 million figure represents roughly 5% of the global population. For comparison, internet users reached similar penetration levels around 2001. If crypto wallet adoption follows a similar growth curve, the number of wallets could exceed 1 billion by 2028, according to projections by Crypto.com.
Wallet diversity matters. The split between exchange-hosted and self-custody wallets reflects different user needs. Casual users and traders prefer exchange wallets for convenience. DeFi users and privacy-conscious holders prefer self-custody. Institutional investors require regulated custody with insurance coverage. This segmentation is driving specialisation across the wallet ecosystem.
Wallets are evolving from simple key storage tools into comprehensive financial interfaces. Modern wallets allow users to trade, stake, lend, bridge between blockchains, and interact with decentralised applications directly. The growth of fintech unicorns from 20 to over 300 includes several wallet and custody companies. The 420 million user base is the foundation on which the next phase of crypto adoption will be built.
